title: Derived pullback commutes with derived tensor product on the constructible categories
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ inside $\Qlb$, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the coefficient categories and operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], with the finite bounded constructible category of [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], the derived-complete integral category of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], the rationalization of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], and the common-stage category of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients].

For $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ and arbitrary $M,N\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})$, there is a canonical isomorphism
$$
 \mu_{f;M,N}:Lf^*(M\otimes^L_\Lambda N)\xrightarrow{\sim}Lf^*M\otimes^L_\Lambda Lf^*N
$$
in the ambient derived category $D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_{E,n})$. In particular this applies to $M,N\in D^b_c(Y,A_{E,n})$, without asserting that their derived tensor product is bounded.

For $\Lambda\in\{\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$ and $M,N\in D^b_c(Y,\Lambda)$, the same formula is an isomorphism in $D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$; the integral tensor product is the completed derived tensor product specified in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. At finite level $\mu$ is the canonical tensor comparison for the morphism of ringed topoi induced by $f$. At integral level it is the functorial derived inverse limit of the finite comparisons on $M_n=M\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}$ and $N_n=N\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}$, using the canonical reduction identifications for completed pullback and tensor. At rational level it is the image of the integral comparison; at the $\Qlb$ level it is represented by the rational comparison over any common finite coefficient field, composed with the scalar-extension comparisons of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension].

These isomorphisms are natural in $M,N$, compatible with associativity, the signed commutativity and the unit isomorphisms of derived tensor, and compatible with composition: for $h:Z\to X$, $\mu_{f\circ h;M,N}$ is $\mu_{h;Lf^*M,Lf^*N}\circ Lh^*(\mu_{f;M,N})$ under the canonical composition identifications of pullbacks. They commute with finite reduction (including the derived change of coefficients $A_{E,m}\to A_{E,n}$ for $m\geq n$) and with scalar extension through finite coefficient field extensions and into $\Qlb$.

source.place: Lemma 21.18.4 (Tag 07A4, label lemma-pullback-tensor-product), for the morphism of ringed topoi (X_proet, (A_{E,n})_X) -> (Y_proet, (A_{E,n})_Y); the integral, rational and Qlbar levels follow the level-by-level definitions of the operations in def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom

proof.text: At finite level choose compatible small representatives of the pro-etale sites as in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. The inverse image and its constant-ring map make $f_n$ a morphism of ringed topoi. By [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact], module pullback is exact and agrees with inverse image with the coefficient action transported through $f^{-1}(A_{E,n})_Y\cong(A_{E,n})_X$. Thus its derived functor is precisely the finite operation in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] with $R=(A_{E,n})_Y$ and $S=(A_{E,n})_X$. Its displayed isomorphism, natural in both arguments, is $\mu_{f;M,N}$. That theorem is unbounded, so it applies to all the finite-level inputs claimed here; no finite Tor dimension of $A_{E,n}$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), applied to the small pro-etale ringed topoi

proof.text: Choose flat-term K-flat resolutions $P,Q$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The closure assertion [lem-pur-kflat-total-tensor-model] shows that $\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes Q)$ is K-flat with flat terms, so all iterated tensors below compute derived tensors. On these models the comparison is totalized from the module map of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor], with the signed differential from [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves].

Use the chain maps of [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence]. Their pure-tensor formula and inverse are the ordinary comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor], and the chain lemma supplies associativity, signed symmetry, units, composition and coefficient-change equations. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] these maps and equations descend from the K-flat resolving class to arbitrary finite-level derived inputs.

source.place: Tag 07A4, total-complex construction and resolving-class descent

proof.text: For integral $M,N$, choose flat-term K-flat representatives $P,Q$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Set $P_n=P\otimes_{R_Y}B_{Y,n}$ and $Q_n=Q\otimes_{R_Y}B_{Y,n}$, with actual quotient transitions. Put $T_n=\operatorname{Tot}(P_n\otimes Q_n)$, $U_n=f_n^*P_n$, $V_n=f_n^*Q_n$, and $W_n=\operatorname{Tot}(U_n\otimes V_n)$. The quotient and pullback models are flat-term K-flat by [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat], and the tensor totals by step 2. The normalization and coherent reduction assertions of [lem-pur-completed-operation-tower-substitution] and [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity] identify these systems with the reductions of the completed operations in [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Here $B_{Y,n}=(A_{E,n})_Y$ and $R_Y=\varprojlim B_{Y,n}$, as in the normalized tower convention [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower].

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 0G7E (lemma-pullback-K-flat), 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product); coherent quotient towers and normalized DVR effectivity

proof.text: The cochain maps of [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence] give the strict tower isomorphism $f_n^*T_n\to W_n$ and its strict inverse. Apply [lem-pur-integral-tower-limit-comparison] to the $T,U,V$ of step 4. With the substitution identifications of [lem-pur-completed-operation-tower-substitution], its actual derived-limit map is the required comparison between completed pullback of $M\widehat\otimes^L N$ and completed tensor of $Lf^*M,Lf^*N$. The functor is [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]; its naturality and the resolution comparisons of [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined] give naturality in $M,N$ and independence of the chosen representatives.

source.place: Tag 07A4, strict quotient comparison; completed-operation substitution

proof.text: By [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible], $M\widehat\otimes^L N$ is constructible on $Y$ and its pullback is constructible on $X$. The same lemma first puts $Lf^*M,Lf^*N$ in $D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ and then puts their completed tensor there. This is a full subcategory of the ambient derived category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], so the ambient comparison and its inverse are morphisms of that subcategory.

The finite associativity, signed symmetry, unit and pullback-composition equations from [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence] are compatible with every quotient transition. The tower-level assertion [lem-pur-integral-coherence-tower] therefore identifies them as equalities of strict normalized systems and gives their integral images after applying [lem-pur-completed-operation-tower-substitution] and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit].

source.place: Tag 07A4, chain coherence realized on normalized systems

proof.text: The coherent counit comparisons of [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity], applied to the source and target systems of the strict comparison, identify its reduction with the finite comparison. Their naturality applies to this actual map of systems, and [lem-pur-completed-operation-tower-substitution] carries the counits to the completed operations. No faithfulness assertion for individual finite-reduction functors is needed.

source.place: Coherent normalized-tower counits and reduction of the strict comparison

proof.text: For $E\subset L$ put $B_m=\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^m$. The strict quotient models of [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension] and the coherent reduction model [lem-pur-coefficient-extension-reduction-model] give the normalized $B_\bullet$-tower, including ramified extensions. The quotient K-flatness is [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings], and the scalar-association and transition equations are exactly [lem-pur-scalar-extension-tower-coherence].

source.place: Quotient scalar-extension models and successive derived coefficient normalization

proof.text: Use the pullback and tensor scalar-extension isomorphisms of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension] in their canonical quotient-model form. The tower coherence statement [lem-pur-scalar-extension-tower-coherence] says that both routes around the comparison square send $b\otimes(x\otimes y)$ to $(b\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$ and commute with every quotient and coefficient square. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] and [lem-pur-completed-operation-tower-substitution] gives the integral scalar-extension square.

source.place: Canonical quotient comparisons and strict system scalar-extension square

proof.text: By [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], every rational object is an integral object and every morphism is a finite sum of $u\otimes a$, with $u$ integral and $a\in E$. Define $\mu^E$ to be the image $\mu^{\mathcal O_E}\otimes1$; its inverse is the image of the integral inverse. The operations on rational morphisms are the scalar extensions specified in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. The integral naturality identity for $u,v$, multiplied by the corresponding scalars, gives rational naturality; add the resulting identities for sums. Every integral coherence equation remains an equality after tensoring Hom groups with $E$, so the rational associativity, symmetry, unit and composition equations follow. The scalar-extension square of the preceding scalar-extension steps likewise remains commutative, since the rational scalar-extension functor is the one induced from the integral scalar-extension functor.

source.place: The raw scalar-localization definition: Hom tensor E; all identities are images of the integral identities

proof.text: For objects $(E,M),(E',N)$ at the algebraically closed level, choose a common finite coefficient field $L$ and form the rational comparison there, conjugated by the scalar-extension comparisons as prescribed in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Represent the inverse by the inverse rational comparison with the inverse conjugating comparisons. In [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], morphisms are classes over common finite fields, and two representatives agree if they agree after passage to a further common field. The scalar-extension calculation after rationalization says precisely that passing from $L$ to any larger field sends this comparison to the same comparison there; hence the class and its inverse are independent of $L$. Represent any finite naturality or coherence diagram over a single common finite field; the rational identity proved in the preceding rationalization step gives its equality in the colimit Hom group. This proves all the asserted compatibilities at $\Qlb$, including scalar extension into $\Qlb$.
